correctness.rationale: Necessary and sufficient connected-domination and inclusion-minimality arguments give an explicit bijection for every finite connected simple base graph of order at least three. The selected originals form a connected vertex cover, internal selected subdivision vertices form a spanning tree, each omitted original gets one boundary selected subdivision vertex, and tree leaves require an external neighbor. The singleton star and two-vertex exceptions are handled separately. The matrix-tree/rank-one determinant calculation yields the all-parameter Stirling counts. Direct independent graph-level exhaustive tests recovered the exact sets on 47 general base graphs and the exact coefficient distributions on seven complete-bipartite cases (1,280,106 tested subsets), with 144 further arithmetic parameter cases. Finite checks are corroboration, not an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The general triple correspondence is an exact structural reduction between minimal connected domination of every full edge subdivision and degree-constrained spanning-tree counting over connected vertex covers. The complete-bipartite specialization determines all cardinality multiplicities. The K_{2,b} family yields connected bipartite 2-degenerate examples with only two minimal connected-domination sizes and a provably absent interval of length b-3. This sharply exposes a sparsity-vs-cardinality phenomenon and goes beyond minimum-value calculations or the preexisting rook-graph Stirling kernel.
